claims.text: The initial intermediate layer is an equiatomic TaNbWMo refractory high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy is homogenized, has an approximately 10 μm grain size, and contains no secondary phases.
The intervention adds 5 at.% Ag to equiatomic TaNbWMo.
Aging the Ag-modified alloy at 500 °C for 4 h precipitates Ag-rich particles along grain boundaries.
The Ag-rich precipitates form an interconnected, percolating network along grain boundaries and triple junctions.
Ag precipitates have sufficiently high intrinsic thermal conductivity to improve heat transfer in the TaNbWMo matrix.
The interconnected Ag-rich network provides continuous percolation paths for phonon and electron heat transport.
Interfaces between the Ag-rich precipitates and the TaNbWMo matrix are coherent.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces maintain load transfer and limit the loss of yield strength.
Adding 5 at.% Ag raises thermal conductivity by at least 15% at 600–800 °C.
Adding 5 at.% Ag reduces yield strength by no more than 10%.
The baseline TaNbWMo intermediate layer has a thermal conductivity of approximately 15 W/m·K at 600 °C.
The Ag-modified layer will have a thermal conductivity of at least 17.3 W/m·K at 600 °C.
The baseline TaNbWMo layer has a room-temperature 0.2% proof stress of approximately 600 MPa.
The claimed performance holds in inert gas at 600–800 °C under cyclic mechanical loads up to 10 MPa.
Ag coarsening during extended high-temperature service could reduce the connectivity of the Ag-rich network.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires at least a 15% conductivity increase and no more than a 10% strength reduction, but the experiment declares falsification only below a 5% conductivity increase or above a 15% strength reduction. Results of 5–15% conductivity improvement or 10–15% strength loss would violate the stated hypothesis without meeting the stated falsification rule.
